cover.title: Freakonomics
cover.author: Steven D. Levitt & Stephen J. Dubner

segments.text: For decades, the Ku Klux Klan's power wasn't rope or fire. It was secrecy. You feared what you couldn't see.
So how do you beat a group whose whole power is a secret? You make the secret worthless.
In 1946, activists fed the Klan's secret passwords to the Superman radio show. Millions of kids heard them on primetime.
By morning, kids were shouting those secret passwords in backyards like a game. The terror became a joke. Sunlight is a weapon.
